_comment: THE SERVICE AND ENVIRONMENT CATALOG, as a repository declaration.
Program 3 names a 'service/environment catalog' among its nine elements. It
existed as PROSE in the Program 0 release-truth inventory and as frozen JSON
contracts under control-room/contracts/, and as zero rows anywhere. This file
is the declaration; tools/ops-record.py --sync-registry applies it into
ops.service and ops.service_environment. Never hand-edit those tables: the
repo is the source and the database is the render, which is the same posture
every other registry in this system takes.
WHY environment IS 'production' FOR JOBS THAT RUN ON JOE'S MAC. The launchd
jobs are local edge agents by the BDUF's definition, but every one of them
reads and writes the PRODUCTION record layer. The environment field answers
'what was affected', not 'what machine was it typed on' — a Control Room
asking which environment last night's export damaged wants the first answer.
The machine is carried by runtime instead.
CADENCE IS WHAT MAKES SILENCE DETECTABLE, so every scheduled service declares
one, and the grace is sized to the real schedule rather than to the ideal:
rules-refresh runs hourly between 07:00 and 20:00, so its true worst-case gap
is the ELEVEN HOURS overnight, and a 3600s cadence would read stale every
morning by design. local-briefs runs weekdays only and its grace spans the
weekend stand-down, the same lesson tools/health-check.py already learned the
expensive way. A cadence that cries wolf nightly is worse than none: it
trains people to stop reading alarms.
A SERVICE WITH NO CADENCE IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. carr-mcp is not scheduled, so
nothing about it goes stale on a clock; its health comes from synthetic
golden-workflow checks, and until those run it reads unknown — which is the
honest answer for a service nobody has observed.
_comment_scheduled_tasks: THE CLAUDE CODE SCHEDULED TASKS (Program 3, 2026-08-14), registered below
the launchd services. One service per task, keyed IDENTICALLY to the
task's own directory name under ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<key>/SKILL.md
(that is also the taskId the scheduler reports and the name the launch
marker in each session's own transcript carries) — no separate mapping
table exists to fall out of sync with either. runtime is
'claude-code-scheduled-task': these are prompts a Claude session executes,
not a script with an exit code, so hooks/scheduled-run-record.py (a Stop
hook) derives the outcome from the session's own transcript
deterministically and records it here — see lib/scheduled_run.py.
nightly-record-layer (above, under the launchd services) already exists as
a service for the launchd chain bin/nightly.sh runs; it is NOT duplicated
here. The Claude session that LAUNCHES that chain is recorded under that
SAME service but the fixed run_key 'scheduled-session' (see
lib/scheduled_run.py RUN_KEY), distinct from the chain's own 'nightly.*'
step keys, so the two can never collide.
ONLY THE CURRENTLY-ENABLED TASKS ARE REGISTERED. x-reply-run-daily,
linkedin-engagement-daily and calendar-fetch-daily are disabled
(`list_scheduled_tasks`, checked 2026-08-14) and deliberately left
unregistered: a cadence-bound service for a task nobody is running would
read STALE forever, which is exactly the false-alarm failure mode
local-briefs' grace design and the launchd services above already learned
to avoid. Register one when its task is re-enabled — sync-registry retires
a service that leaves this file, never the reverse, so nothing is lost by
waiting.
CADENCE for the weekly tasks uses the SAME 604800s/172800s (7 day cadence,
2 day grace) local-briefs already established for a task that can miss its
one weekly window if the Mac is asleep; the monthly tasks (which actually
fire once inside a several-day window via their own internal ledger gate,
per each SKILL.md) use 2592000s/518400s so the window itself is not
mistaken for drift.

services.name: Partner interrupt channel
services.purpose: The Joe/Dell interrupt poll.

environments.notes: Wakes every two minutes, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval (Program 4 follow-up) throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 1800s — recording all ~720 fires/day as rows would be pure noise from a healthy channel. Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle, so cadence here reflects the succeeded heartbeat, not the wake. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18: the succeeded row now rides the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and is inserted at the next run-spool-flush, up to 1800s after the throttle emitted it, so the honest worst-case gap between inserts is throttle+flush (3600s) against a window of cadence+grace (4500s). Also 2026-08-18: the plist passes --scheduled, which skips the QUERY (never the wake, never the row) outside weekdays 07:00-19:00 local — the last thing keeping the Neon compute from autosuspending. The 2-minute interrupt Joe promised on 2026-08-03 is unchanged during the working day; outside it the job still wakes, still exits 0, and still records its heartbeat through the spool, so this service and carr-local-edge-node stay observable overnight exactly as before. This job once logged 382 consecutive identical 'nothing new' lines to a local log with a broken query, because a channel with nothing to say and a channel that cannot ask produce byte-identical output — a run row (even throttled) still distinguishes them, since a genuinely broken query fails loud and goes to the ledger direct, ahead of the spool.

Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18 for the spool delay (tools/ops-spool.py): a succeeded row is inserted at the next run-spool-flush, up to 1800s after it was emitted.

The explicit claude-desktop queue target starts a durable Claude background session only after a queue claim, then uses Claude Code's supported /desktop handoff after completion; it is excluded from ordinary conversational fan-out. On the same existing wake, the separate lease-bound Engineering Passport controller may drain one already-admitted engineering-slice job through the fixed fresh Codex desk; it never creates work or exposes its carr_jobs credential to that desk. Queue projection alone uses the locked, shape-checked project-room-queue door; ordinary room traffic remains on the local-machine identity. The live wire between the room and the desks registered in ~/.config/carr/hermes-desks.json.

environments.notes: Wakes every 60s, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 900s (15 min) — recording all ~1440 fires/day would be noise from a quiet room, the same reasoning capture-poll and partner-ping already state above. Every FAILURE (e.g. read-room unreachable) is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle. Cadence/grace mirror capture-poll's own widened figures for the same tools/ops-spool.py flush-delay reason: a succeeded row can land up to ~1800s after the throttle emitted it.

The daily cadence and weekend-spanning grace make the Mac edge lifecycle visible without treating an installed plist as activation authority. services.name: Canonical checkout and configuration fleet sync
services.purpose: Fast-forwards each Mac's canonical main checkout only when the fail-closed local-state proof accepts it, then re-renders repository-owned configuration.

environments.notes: Fires hourly (StartCalendarInterval at :31, lib/launchd_calendar.py) and again at RunAtLoad (login/wake), changed 2026-09-23 from four fixed daily fires so a Mac asleep or unused for a stretch catches up immediately instead of reading up to twelve hours stale. Cadence is 3600s; 3600s grace covers launch delay and the local spool's next-flush delay, matching the grace already used by this repo's other hourly local jobs (e.g. notes-sweep). The plist routes through bin/run-scheduled.sh as service fleet-sync with run key fleet.sync, and now also fast-forwards the sibling checkouts declared in ops/config/fleet-sync-siblings.json (doctorcre-app, software-factory) under the same fail-closed contract; a sibling's own outcome is reported but never affects this service's own run status. This declaration makes the job representable; it does not claim the LaunchAgent is installed or loaded, or that ops.service has been synced.

services.name: Joe's Mac — local edge node presence
services.purpose: The registered fact of this Mac's own presence, per PROP-010 (deterministic recurring work runs from versioned repo code executed by a registered Local Edge Node through launchd). Not a job's business outcome — a heartbeat that this machine is awake, Joe is logged in, and launchd is actually waking its agents. A sleeping, logged-out, FileVault-locked, or otherwise unreachable Mac must read stale or unknown here, never healthy.

environments.notes: Recorded by bin/run-scheduled.sh's --also-heartbeat flag, riding partner-ping's own 2-minute launchd wake as an independent second provenance line (key=launchd.heartbeat), throttled to at most one succeeded row per 1800s by the SAME --heartbeat-interval — regardless of whether the partner-ping buzz query itself succeeds. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18 for the spool delay (tools/ops-spool.py): the row is inserted at the next run-spool-flush. A Mac that is asleep or logged out stops waking the LaunchAgent at all, so this service goes stale within 4500s (75 min) of the last real wake rather than reading healthy on a stopped clock — the price of letting Neon autosuspend between flushes, accepted in the 2026-08-18 cloud-usage decision.

services.name: CARR control-plane ledger tick
services.purpose: Local launchd adapter that gives the job ledger a once-per-minute opportunity to enqueue due work. It does not execute workflows or own their schedules.

environments.notes: Definition only: this repository change neither installs nor enables the agent. The tick has no ops.run heartbeat because it is itself a jobs-role ledger client; its durable effect is the idempotent ledger enqueue, and legacy schedules remain independently active until accepted cutover evidence and approval.

NOT YET INSTALLED (built in worktree cutover-watch, 2026-08-27) — the orchestrating session installs it after this branch merges to main; see tools/scheduler-truth.py's INSTALL_EXEMPT for the same statement in machine-checkable form.

services.purpose: Deletes call recordings past their retention window.

services.name: Run-row spool flusher
services.purpose: The one scheduled door between the local run-row spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and the Neon ledger. Replays queued heartbeat rows through tools/ops-record.py in one batch every 30 minutes, which is what lets the database autosuspend between batches instead of being held awake by a recording every few minutes (2026-08-18 cloud-usage audit).

environments.notes: Criticality HIGH although the job is small: every wrapper-recorded service's freshness now depends on this one draining the queue, so a silently stopped flusher would age every heartbeat at once. Its OWN succeeded row rides the spool it just drained and lands on the NEXT flush — hence a grace wider than its cadence: the steady-state gap between its inserts is one full flush interval plus the next flush's delay. A genuinely failed flush is state=failed and goes to the ledger direct (the spool tries failures direct first), so a broken flusher does not have to wait for itself to be reported.

services.name: Canonical checkout fast-forward
services.purpose: WR-000040 AC-FRESH. Keeps the shared checkout at ~/carr-system within one day of origin/main, and never buys that with somebody's edit: it refuses on tracked modifications, refuses off main, refuses when canonical is ahead, and its only branch-moving command is `git merge --ff-only`. No reset, no checkout of a path, no clean, no stash. See lib/canonical_freshness.py, reached through tools/repo-hygiene-janitor.py --canonical-freshness fast-forward.

environments.notes: Daily at 03:20 local, per Joe's AC-FRESH cadence ruling (decision fa8ae14b-e6fe-4e1b-ae98-0b6eb5a255f8, 2026-09-11). Grace is 1.25x the cadence because a succeeded row rides the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and lands at the next run-spool-flush, up to ~1800s after the fire. A REFUSAL IS NOT A FAILURE OF THIS SERVICE: exit 3 (tracked dirt), 4 (ahead of origin) and 7 (wrong branch) mean the job correctly declined to move somebody's tree, and com.carr.canonical-dirty-watchdog is the surface that pages about the condition. This service going quiet is what matters here, which is why it has a cadence at all.

services.name: Scripted release pipeline (Worker + DoctorCRE app)
services.purpose: Decisions 17ef11fa/b729859d: release is script-triggered. Every minute compares each lane's origin/main with the last SHA it released and, when the batch touches release paths, runs the sanctioned manual release sequence unattended from a detached worktree at the exact SHA (staging replacement, staging app writer, migrate-prod, deploy-worker upload/staging/promote, live readback, health; credential-free node scripts/prepare-release.mjs, then provider-only node scripts/release-production.mjs for the app). Stops on any nonzero exit, records the step and log, never retries that SHA, and enqueues a repo-write Model Room diagnosis session to fix forward by PR. Kill switch: ops/config/release-pipeline.v1.json enabled, or ~/.config/carr/release-pipeline.off. See ops/release-pipeline.py.

environments.notes: Wakes every 60s; bin/run-scheduled.sh --heartbeat-interval 3600 throttles SUCCEEDED rows to one an hour, and every failure (a stopped release, or exit 3 for a missing unattended credential) is recorded immediately. Grace covers the ops-spool flush delay, as for room-bridge. What shipped, failed or blocked is in out/release-pipeline/releases.jsonl; `ops/release-pipeline.py report --date D` prints it for a daily note.

services.name: Canonical checkout dirty/staleness watchdog
services.purpose: WR-000040 AC-FRESH, the alarm half. Observes the canonical checkout ALONE — it never calls the fast-forward and never reads anything the fast-forward wrote — so it still pages when that agent is unloaded, its program is missing, or the machine slept through every window. Pages on an unobservable repository, tracked dirt, a branch other than main, staleness past the 24h bar, canonical holding commits origin/main does not have, and an unverifiable fetch. Untracked paths are counted and named, never alarmed: AC-CLEAN routes those to Joe per path.

environments.notes: Hourly, per the same AC-FRESH cadence ruling. Criticality HIGH although the job only reads: it is the only surface that reports the fast-forward never having fired, and launchd says nothing when it drops an agent. It pages by two independent routes — a report-problem record through run.sh, and a nonzero exit that this wrapper turns into a failed run row — so an unreachable store cannot silence it. Grace is 1.5x the cadence for the same spool delay as its sibling.

services.name: Gate Zero scheduler canary
services.purpose: The no-op job whose only product is proof that the scheduler ran it. Gate Zero's fourth predecessor step, step:scheduler-active-receipt, needs an ops.run row bound to a receipt — non-null evidence_ref, written by bin/run-scheduled.sh with source_kind wrapper — plus an observation strictly after that dispatch; mcp-server/src/gate-zero-seam-readers.v5.js is the reader that judges it. Measured 2026-09-11 against production: 28,309 runs, 21,894 of them from the wrapper, and ZERO carrying an evidence_ref, so the clause was unsatisfiable by any row in the ledger's history rather than merely unmet. WHY A DEDICATED JOB: a real job's row conflates 'the scheduler fired' with 'the work succeeded', and a red row cannot be read for the first without knowing the second. This job has no work to fail at, so its row is a clean statement about the scheduler alone.

environments.notes: NOT YET ACTIVATED, deliberately: the plist is held in DEFINITION_ONLY in lib/launchd_hold.py, so installing it is Joe's own act and its presence in ~/Library/LaunchAgents is a drift finding until he takes it off that list. Until then this service has no runs and reads unknown — the honest answer for a job nobody has started, and the same posture carr-mcp already takes. CRITICALITY IS LOW because nothing depends on the canary's own work: it has none. What depends on it is one gate's ability to ask a question, and that gate reads a missing canary correctly today. Grace 5400s against a 3600s cadence covers the 30-minute run-spool flush (tools/ops-spool.py) exactly as notes-sweep's and run-spool-flush's graces do: a succeeded row queues locally and lands at the next flush, so the worst honest gap is one interval plus one flush.

services.name: Logitech modifier-key repair
services.purpose: Re-applies the hidutil modifier mapping, which dies on reboot and on receiver replug.

environments.notes: Wakes every 10 min and is idempotent by design, so a missed pass costs a keyboard that behaves oddly until the next one. The cadence is deliberately 2h rather than 10 min, with run-scheduled.sh's heartbeat throttle doing the same job it does for capture-poll: recording 144 identical successes a day would be noise, and a low-criticality cosmetic repair does not earn a row that goes stale within the hour.

services.name: Record-derived egress host allowlist
services.purpose: Regenerates the machine-local host allowlist so the egress guard does not silently fall back to the code list.

environments.notes: NO CADENCE ON PURPOSE, and this one is not a scheduled job that happens to lack a schedule. The plist is SECONDARY MACHINE ONLY: on Joe's primary Mac the allowlist is regenerated as a step of the nightly chain, so this agent is deliberately not installed here and a cadence would report it missing every single day on the one machine where its absence is correct. It is registered so the service EXISTS in the catalog for the machines that do run it.

services.name: Call-mode dictation server
services.purpose: Long-running server backing meeting capture; holds the recording session state.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server, so the health question is 'is it up' and never 'did it fire recently'. bin/probe-keepalive.py answers it every 10 min by opening a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:4682 — a connect proves it is ACCEPTING, which is a real answer rather than a PID sighting. Still exempt from bin/run-scheduled.sh: the wrapper records on child exit, and a KeepAlive child exiting means launchd restarted it. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18: an UP row rides the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and is inserted at the next run-spool-flush, up to 1800s after the probe saw it; a DOWN row still goes to the ledger direct and becomes an incident on the spot.

services.name: Doc conversation server
services.purpose: Long-running local server for the Doc conversational surface.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server. Probed every 10 min by a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:4680, which proves it is ACCEPTING rather than merely running. Same wrapper exemption and the same reason as call-mode; same 2026-08-18 grace widening (900→2700) for the spool delay — an UP row lands at the next run-spool-flush, a DOWN row still lands direct. Proven end to end on 2026-08-14: stopping the agent produced SEV-3 INC-20260814-08 within one probe pass, and restarting it moved the incident to monitoring.

services.name: Desk dictation agent
services.purpose: Phase B desk dictation, distinct from meeting-mode consent capture.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server with NO PORT TO KNOCK ON, so its probe is process liveness only — a weaker claim than the other two, and the run detail says which signal was used so the row is never read as more than it is. A wedged process and a healthy one both have a PID. Same wrapper exemption and reason as call-mode; same 2026-08-18 grace widening (900→2700) for the spool delay.

services.name: Notes-sweep canary ingest sink
services.purpose: Isolated loopback-only ingest destination that proves the notes-sweep CANARY's whole posting path (auth, body shape, external_id dedup) without touching the live ingest socket.

environments.notes: KeepAlive server, same shape as doc-engine and call-mode: the health question is 'is it up', never 'did it fire recently', so it is probed by bin/probe-keepalive.py opening a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:4684 rather than by recent-run freshness — a connect proves it is ACCEPTING. Same wrapper exemption and reason as the other two KeepAlive servers: bin/run-scheduled.sh records on child exit, and a KeepAlive child exiting just means launchd restarted it. Refuses to bind unless a mode-0600 credential file is present, so it will show DOWN until ~/.config/carr/notes-canary.env exists — that is a config precondition, not a service defect.

services.name: Recording capture bridge, claim side
services.purpose: Claims new recording sessions as they appear under ~/Recordings.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered, so SILENCE IS THE NORMAL STATE — it fires only when a recording session starts. Any cadence would cry wolf on every day Joe records nothing, which is most days, and an alarm that fires on a quiet day is how both partners learn to stop reading alarms.

services.name: Recording consent announcer
services.purpose: Plays the all-party consent announcement when a recording session begins.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered; silence is normal, so no cadence. Criticality is HIGH despite being a small watcher: it is what makes the rig announce recording aloud, and Florida is an all-party-consent state. A failure here is a legal exposure rather than an inconvenience, which is why it is registered even though nothing can currently observe it firing.

services.name: Video encode watcher
services.purpose: Encodes video dropped into the CARR Video Pipeline intake folder.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered; silence is normal, so no cadence. Its script lives OUTSIDE the repo, under ~/Movies, which means it is not version-controlled and would not survive the Mac — worth naming here because the catalog is where that kind of exposure becomes visible.

services.name: KeepAlive server liveness probe
services.purpose: Asks the three long-running servers whether they are up, and writes the answer to the ledger.

environments.notes: Wakes every 10 min; cadence declared at 30 min so one missed pass is not an alarm. It is itself wrapped by bin/run-scheduled.sh, because a watcher whose own failure is invisible is the one thing nothing watches. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18 for the spool delay (tools/ops-spool.py). It returns EX_CONFIG (78) rather than a failure when NOTHING could be recorded at all — since the spool, that means the local recording path itself is broken (not even the SQLite queue writable), not merely an unreachable database — and a probe that alarmed every 10 minutes on a Mac in that state would be the smoke-suite mistake again.

services.name: Cloud nightly backup (GitHub Actions)
services.purpose: The GitHub-hosted Nightly backup (cloud) workflow and its exact failure/disabled/artifact evidence contract; registered so supervised observer-qualified failures can be filed under their true service identity rather than nightly-record-layer.

environments.notes: Externally scheduled by GitHub Actions daily at 02:35 UTC. GitHub native failure email reports a failed run; it does not detect a missed or skipped schedule. GitHub runs are not continuously ingested into ops.run, so expected_cadence_seconds is omitted and CARR service-environment health remains unknown. Missed-run freshness is evaluated separately when the Mac-local nightly-record-layer invokes ops/recovery-point.py on its host-local daily 02:05 schedule. recovery-point.py applies RPO_HOURS=24 to the newest qualified artifact; provider/API unreadability remains unknown. nightly-record-layer's cadence_grace_seconds=7200 is service-health grace, not a guaranteed consumer observation or alert-delivery bound. Observation delay depends on host availability and the timestamp of the last qualified artifact. This is consumer observation, not service cadence ingestion.

services.name: Job watchdog
services.purpose: Scan registered jobs, head-bound pull requests, merge-queue failures and release logs; report findings to the orchestrator and dispatch deterministic recovery actions.

environments.notes: Primary-only schedule. Cadence is a checked projection of ops/config/job-watchdog.json. This draft ships source definitions; the orchestrator owns activation and replacement of the scratch auto-enqueue process. Findings and dated scan completion ledger are durable; scanner makes no model judgments.

services.name: Session trace archive
services.purpose: Nightly local archive of CARR-scoped Claude Code and Codex session transcripts (lib/carr_session_scope.py decides scope; nothing else is archived) as gzip .jsonl.gz into ~/carr-local/session-trace-archive/, so old sessions the clients prune are not lost. Streams bytes only; reads no transcript content beyond a Codex session's cwd metadata line.

environments.notes: Daily at 03:10 local, plus RunAtLoad. Per-machine by design (both the source transcripts and the destination archive are local to whichever Mac runs it), so it is neither PRIMARY_ONLY nor SECONDARY_ONLY in ops/config-as-code.py, and it depends on nothing in the record layer — no dependencies entry below.

services.name: Expert reply watch
services.purpose: Weekly read-only mining of tracked X accounts replies into queued log-capture records, with URL deduplication and a dated local run ledger.

environments.notes: Monday 06:00 local. Primary only; Grok stdout proposals pass deterministic validation. CLI failure records one defect and exits nonzero. No X writes.

dependencies.note: The local adapter schedules, claims, and completes only the receipt-gated prebrief jobs lease.
The checkout sync is local and fail-closed; its generic ops.run receipt is projected through the record layer by the existing run-scheduled spool path.
Every poll cycle reads/writes the partner room through the deployed Worker (tools/call-verb.py) — no direct database connection.
The ledger is the tick's sole authority and state owner.
